notes.deenhindi-nasai:2619: Both full fields were read. Abu Hurayrah reports the actual sermon, annual-obligation question repeated three times, silence and the complete conditional reply. Keep the if-yes/then-obligatory/then-unable sequence, the leave-until-addressed qualification, the earlier peoples' excessive questions/disagreement account, the ability limit on commanded actions and the prohibition clause. The Urdu footnote locator alone is context. No external legal elaboration or absent commentary is added.
notes.deenhindi-nasai:2621: Both complete originals were read. Urdu gives the old father's inability to perform Hajj, Umrah or travel, followed by the actual reply to act for him. Hindi has a damaged predicate after old father and omits part of the inability/Hajj clause; retain its own finite question/reply fragment with an explicit wording qualification, without filling its gap from Urdu. Both retain the on-father's-behalf relation and the reply's Hajj-and-Umrah scope. Urdu's footnote marker is context.
notes.deenhindi-ibnmajah:2554: Both complete originals contain the actual historical Maiz encounter: four confessions and repeated turning away, the order, the flight when struck, the unnamed man's camel-jawbone blow, the later reporting and the final why-did-you-not-leave-him question. Preserve every supplied repetition, actor relation, condition and actual response. This is attributed historical narration, not a new present-day instruction. No explanatory appendix, variant apparatus or long prefatory chain is present.
notes.deenhindi-ibnmajah:2560: Both full originals were read. Qasim reports Ibn Abbas mentioning two people performing lian; the actual Shaddad-labelled question expressly embeds the conditional Prophetic quotation, and Ibn Abbas then gives his own reply. Preserve the separate setting/question-with-quotation/Companion-answer voices in source order. Hindi says Shaddad whereas Urdu says Ibn Shaddad, and Hindi's final descriptor is damaged; keep each own spelling without identity repair or an Urdu-derived replacement. Do not merge Ibn Abbas's answer with the Prophet's quoted conditional statement.
